Hyperdulia
hī-per-doo´lee-a
n. (Rome's third rank of religious honour: above the dulia of saints, below the latria of God, assigned to Mary; a distinction the second commandment does not know)
Greek hyper, above, + douleia, service, bondage, religious honour. Medieval Catholic theology ranked latria (God), dulia (saints), and hyperdulia (Mary). The New Testament knows one worship-word for God, and an angel who will not take it.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Hyperdulia is the Roman name for a rank of honour invented to give Mary more than the saints and less than God. The Scriptures do not furnish the rank. “Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve” (Mat 4:10). The first commandment is not a spectrum: “Thou shalt have no other gods before me” (Exo 20:3). The LORD will not share: “my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images” (Isa 42:8). When John fell down before an angel, the angel refused even that: “See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant... worship God” (Rev 19:10). Peter did the same with Cornelius: “Stand up; I myself also am a man” (Act 10:26). If an apostle and an angel will not receive what Rome calls dulia, a third rank called hyperdulia is not a solution. It is the same bow with a finer name. Mary is blessed among women. She is not a recipient of religious service. The honour due a fellow-servant is not a rung between latria and the rest of the church.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for hyperdulia. The term is medieval Catholic: a degree of religious honour above dulia and below latria, assigned to the Virgin. The Authorized Version does not know a third rank of worship.

expand to see more

HYPERDULIA, n. [Gr. hyper, above, + douleia, service.]

A medieval Catholic rank of religious honour, above the dulia given to saints and below the latria given to God, assigned to Mary.

Not an 1828 English headword. The distinction is unknown to the second commandment and to the angel of Revelation 19:10.

The dictionary already has latria, dulia, and mariolatry. Hyperdulia is the middle name by which the bow is kept and the commandment is said to be kept also.

Key Scripture

Mat 4:10 — "Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve."

Exo 20:3 — "Thou shalt have no other gods before me."

Isa 42:8 — "I am the LORD: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images."

Rev 19:10 — "And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy."

Act 10:26 — "But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man."

Modern Corruption

A third rank of worship is invented so that the bow toward Mary can be called not-worship. Matthew 4:10 does not offer ranks. It offers only.

expand to see more

The catechetical move is always the same: we do not worship Mary, we give her hyperdulia. Latria is God's. Dulia is the saints'. She gets the extra. Matthew 4:10 does not read, “him only shalt thou serve, excepting a middle honour.” Him only. The angel of Revelation 19:10 will not take what a devout man thought was mere reverence. See thou do it not. Worship God. If the angel will not have it, the mother of the Lord will not have it either, and Luke never shows her receiving it.

Isaiah 42:8 is the end of the argument about images and about persons. My glory will I not give to another. A glory that looks like religious service — candles, invocations, titles of queen of heaven, prayers through her as mediatrix — is already another. Hyperdulia is the word that says it is not. The word is doing the work the commandment forbade.

Honour to Mary as the blessed among women, as the handmaid of the Lord, as a fellow-saint, is not the dispute. Peter said he was a man. So was she. The dictionary's mariolatry entry names the cult. Hyperdulia is the technical name the cult uses to say it is not a cult. Call the bow what the angel called it, and stop.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek hyper + douleia (G1397), service; proskyneō (G4352), to worship; latreuō (G3000), to serve; Hebrew abad / shachah.

expand to see more

Greek proskyneō (G4352) — to worship; Matthew 4:10, Revelation 19:10, the verb Rome splits into ranks.

Greek latreuō (G3000) — to serve; Matthew 4:10, him only.

Greek douleia (G1397) — bondage, service; the root of dulia and hyperdulia, which the New Testament never ranks as religious honours toward creatures.

Usage

"“Him only shalt thou serve” — not him, plus a middle rank."

"“See thou do it not... worship God” — an angel refusing what Rome would call dulia."

"“My glory will I not give to another” — a finer name does not make another less another."
